correctness.rationale: Exact differentiation gives two polynomial balances. Invariance yields the moment laws; monotonicity plus boundedness and uniform continuity gives the T<0 convergence theorem, while the T=0 case uses the second balance and an exact first integral. Sharp Wirtinger plus an equality-case substitution gives the period floor and its strictness for R!=0. Symbolic residuals vanish.

originality.rationale: Historic and modern Moore--Spiegel work covers periodic and aperiodic dynamics, averaging, bifurcations, periodic-orbit expansions, generalized-equation topology, multistability and topological dynamics. The inspected material did not state the exact invariant-measure balances, T<=0 compact-recurrence classification, nonlinear-damping excursion threshold, or global sharp period floor. Full texts of Baker--Moore--Spiegel (1971) and Letellier--Malasoma (2014) were not inspected and remain explicit coverage risks. Originality is to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem constrains all compact recurrent states, not just a selected attractor: it gives exact RMS and higher-moment balances, a global bounded-recurrence obstruction, a physically interpretable damping-threshold excursion, and a sharp parameter-only period lower bound with equality characterized.
